To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
students who are successful in learning programming have a positive attitude toward programming.

the most significant barrier to learning programming for the student is their own fear and anxiety about programming, and that this can be alleviated by using a learning methodology that is student-centered and that allows for self-discovery of programming concepts.

the students who succeed at programming courses are those who have an aptitude for mathematics, are motivated, and have a good grasp of English, and that the best learning tools are those which encourage the students to work on the problem themselves and to learn from their mistakes, and that the students who do not succeed at programming courses do so because of a lack of motivation, a fear of failure, and an inability to cope with abstract concepts.

the barriers to learning to program.
the fear of failure and the fear of success that students experience when they learn programming.
the barriers to learning and the teaching tools which could be employed to overcome these barriers.

there is a need for further research to determine what the best teaching methodologies are for teaching programming.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the student’s level of fear and self-efficacy are the two main factors affecting the learning of programming.
the fear of the programming language, the fear of failure and the lack of confidence of the students are the major factors which affect students learning to program in a tertiary environment.
the student’s fear of failure and the lack of self-efficacy in learning to program are major factors in the student’s ability to learn to program.

the fear of the unknown, and the fear of failing, is a major factor that affects student learning in a tertiary environment.
the fear factor plays a significant role in student success.
the fear factor, in all its manifestations, is a significant barrier to learning programming in the tertiary environment and should be addressed in a variety of ways by educators.
